Trace 1 and Trace 2 both solve the graph coloring problem by identifying node G as a central hub and coloring its neighbors first. Their approaches diverge in verification and solution management. Trace 1 repeatedly re-verifies the full edge list multiple times and flip-flops between two valid solutions before discarding the alternative; this behavior contains a clear CYCLE (exploring an alternative solution and then pruning it) and multiple LOOPs (redundant full edge verifications). Trace 2 is more linear, verifying its solution once before performing a final redundant check, resulting in LOOPs but no CYCLE.

⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Wait, is there any simpler assignment?" end="Both are valid. I will use the first one because I derived it step-by-step and checked it thoroughly." basis=The solver explores an alternative coloring (G=Red, A=Blue, B=Green), verifies it works, but then discards it in favor of the original solution.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's verify each edge one more time with these assignments." end="Solution is valid." basis=The solver re-executes the full edge verification step for the first solution, which was already completed earlier in the trace.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="Let's re-verify the second assignment carefully." end="Everything seems consistent." basis=The solver re-executes the full edge verification process for the second solution, repeating the detailed edge-by-edge check.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's re-verify the first assignment carefully." end="Everything seems correct." basis=The solver re-executes the full edge verification for the first solution yet again, adding no new information.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=clear start="Let's double check the edge list one more time to be absolutely sure." end="This seems solid." basis=The solver re-executes the edge verification step which was already completed earlier in the trace.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=2 conf=probable start="One final check of the graph edges." end="My solution handles all identified triangles correctly." basis=The solver re-verifies the graph constraints (triangles) which were already checked during the solution derivation.
